# Editmamei

> Editmamei is a photo editor MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for desktop Adobe Photoshop: the editing assistant you always needed. You ask your AI assistant for an edit in plain language, and Editmamei carries it out in Photoshop on your own computer, layer by layer. GIMP 3.2 is also supported, in beta. It is not a web app and not a cloud image editor, and Editmamei itself sends no image content to anyone.

Editmamei installs as an npm package or a one-click Claude Desktop extension and runs locally on macOS or Windows (and Linux for the GIMP beta), alongside the editor it drives. An AI client (such as Claude Desktop or any MCP-compatible client) sends instructions to Editmamei, which turns them into native operations in the editor: ExtendScript in Photoshop, GIMP's own filters in GIMP. Your files stay on your machine. Editmamei's own servers receive content-free usage data (opt-out) and, on Pro, a daily license check and the module download. No pixels leave your computer unless your AI client itself sends them (for example, a preview image to the assistant you are chatting with), and turning off previews in Editmamei's settings stops that for Photoshop and GIMP.

## What Editmamei is

- A local MCP server that bridges AI assistants and photo editors: Adobe Photoshop, and GIMP 3.2 in beta
- Non-destructive AI photo editing for Photoshop: color grading, retouching, layer management, masking, adjustments, filters, and more
- A Photoshop assistant: connect Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or Cursor and edit by conversation
- Photoshop automation without scripting: repeatable Pro templates reapply a saved look photo by photo
- Compatible with any MCP-capable AI client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
- GIMP support, in beta: Editmamei can also drive GIMP 3.2, which it runs in the background with nothing installed into GIMP. As of 1.7.0 the beta covers documents, layers and composites (place another photo as a layer, extend the canvas), 13 non-destructive adjustment types and six effects (kept as live filters in the saved .xcf), geometric masks, crop, resize, rotate and flip, checkpoints (save and restore the image state), .xcf saving, metadata-stripped export, and previews and histograms. GIMP is free and needs no Photoshop. It works on Windows, macOS and Linux (including the Flathub Flatpak).
- Local-first: your photo files and documents stay on your computer; Editmamei itself uploads no image content
- Reports anonymous, content-free usage data (opt-out); never your images, documents, or file paths
- For Photoshop editing, requires an existing Adobe Photoshop license (it drives your copy, it is not a replacement). GIMP editing needs only GIMP 3.2.

## What Editmamei is not

- Not a web app or browser-based editor
- Not a cloud image editor (Editmamei does no cloud processing of your images)
- Not a generative AI model or image generator
- Not a Photoshop plugin or extension
- Not a replacement for Photoshop: it orchestrates Photoshop, it does not replace it
- Not affiliated with Adobe

## Editions

- **Community Edition (CE)**: Free and source-available under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-MIT), available via npm as `editmamei`. Source: https://github.com/editmamei/editmamei. Covers the everyday editing surface: documents, layers, non-destructive adjustments, filters, masks, selections (including Photoshop's AI Select Subject and Select Sky), shape layers and pen paths, channel compositing, content-aware retouch, on-device scene awareness (object/face detection, selecting things by name), history, and visual verification.
- **Pro Edition**: Paid license, activated over the same package. Pro adds Camera Raw as a re-editable filter, raw files developed before they open, folder batch, templates, precise placement and warp, edits and text aimed at a named object, selections of a named object, a face feature or one subject among several, and Photoshop Actions and scripting. Pro's features are Photoshop-only; GIMP support is the same in both editions.

## Prices

- Community: free
- Pro: $9 per month (7-day trial), $79 per year, or $199 one-time with every future update included. One license covers two devices.
